sources.citation: Arnold, Laura. 2025 [repository issue date 2024-11-24]. The diachrony of word prosody in the Maˈya-Salawati languages of Raja Ampat. Oceanic Linguistics 64. (Author accepted manuscript, ANU Open Research handle 1885/733807978.)
sources.note: Only a negative, second-hand remark that Esaro (= Duriankere) is 'not tonal' (basis: de Vries 2004 and Verdizade p.c; no data shown); nothing on word stress in Esaro. Recorded here because it is the only printed prosodic characterisation of the language found, but it is not a first-hand stress or tone description and does not fix a stress reading.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2024. The linguistic position of the Inanwatan language of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 42: 237-260. ISSN 0023-1959.
sources.note: Explicit expert statement that NO information on stress exists for Duriankari (or any SBH language other than Inanwatan and Kemberano). The Duriankari content is segmental/historical only: Duriankari did not undergo the Inanwatan merger of oral and nasal phonemes ([n] vs [r,ɾ] and [m] vs [w] contrast both initially and intervocalically: [ini] 'you', [eri] 'two', [rino] 'night', [ni] 'eat', [mi:mo] 'dog', [we:ko] 'fire', p.244); Duriankari retained pSBH *k where Inanwatan has q/ʔ (atoko 'bone', kepo 'foot', kero 'ear', akoro 'female child', p.250); possible separate /s/ < *t assibilation (citi…

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: A comprehensive guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 569-640. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: table row (0 speakers, source Smits & Voorhoeve 1998) and classificatory mention only; the Bird's Head prosody paragraph (p.586) discusses Inanwatan lexical stress (de Vries 2004:25), not Duriankere.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarstrom. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: A comprehensive guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Classificatory listing with speaker number 0 and wordlist sources only; the chapter's prosody section (p.89) discusses Momuna, Una, Marind, Kaure, Fasu, not Duriankere.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen RI). n.d. [c. 2017-2019]. 'Bahasa Efpan' (Provinsi Papua Barat). Peta Bahasa / language-mapping entry idb=576.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: location, ethnic composition (70% Kawit), speaker count, neighbouring languages, dialectometry percentages only.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2004. A short grammar of Inanwatan: an endangered language of the Bird's Head of Papua, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics 560. Canberra: ANU. pp. 1-2, 96.
sources.note: Silent on Duriankere (reports Inanwatan speakers at Seget said in March 1994 the Duriankari language 'was no longer used'). The phonology chapter concerns Inanwatan only ('unpredictable, lexical word stress', p.25) -- a different language (szp).

sources.citation: Remijsen, Bert. 2001. Word-prosodic systems of Raja Ampat languages. LOT 49. Utrecht: LOT. Sec. 2.3.8 p.30.
sources.note: Only sociolinguistic mention: Duriankari (Yefpan) village 'has or used to have its own language.. Papuan', shift to Moi noted by Polansky 1957, probably extinct (de Vries 1998). No data.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part II. Irian Jaya Source Materials 10, Series B-4. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS. (Duriankere list)
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy. access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Only fuller primary record of Duriankere (Anceaux's complete wordlist); if Anceaux marked accent on items, this is the sole place any stress information could survive. No prose rule expected.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU. (language index + author entries)
sources.note: bibliography only: 'Barrs 1978, SH [Silzer & Heikkinen index], Voorhoeve 1975, W&H 1981'; confirms no descriptive work existed by 1995.

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 81-117. Abepura: UNCEN-SIL. Sec. 4.2.2 'Duriankere' p.92; sec. 3.3 'Phonological features' p.89.
sources.note: Silent. Duriankere entry is four sentences (<100 speakers, 'may be a dialect rather than a separate language. We do not have sufficient data to make a judgement'); no Duriankere wordlist collected; sec. 3.3 on the stock mentions only open syllables, few clusters, prenasalised stops.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Sec. 2.6.2.3.4.2 'The Inanwatan Family', pp. 440-441.
sources.note: Silent. Location, 38% cognates with Inanwatan, pronoun table (nani, ani, ani, iganoa, iotokodi, eini, sagan), one verb form mo-na 'come'; 'grammatical information is.. restricted to the pronouns and a few verb forms'. No phonology for Duriankere (by contrast Barau gets 'the accent is a high-pitch accent', p.439).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. Entry 55 Duriankere p.34; 40-item wordlist no. 55 'DURIANKERE (Ac)'.
sources.note: Silent. Entry gives village and source 'U 4' (Anceaux unpublished); 40-word Anceaux list printed without stress marks (memo 'arm', bunakak-o 'ashes', dorimo 'bird'..).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Duriankari'. NewGuineaWorld wiki (Santa Fe Institute / UZH host).
sources.note: 'While there is no published phonology of Duriankari, inspection of the materials in combination with comparison to Inanwatan suggests perhaps 12 consonants and 5 vowels'; nothing on stress. Second-hand.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Duriankari language'.
sources.note: Nothing; extinct; cites Voorhoeve 1975, Berry & Berry 1987, de Vries 2004, Smits & Voorhoeve 1998.

sources.citation: Polansky, 1957. [Dutch administrative memorandum on Salawati / Radja Ampat] (cited by Remijsen 2001:30 for Duriankari language shift).

sources.note: Earliest report on the Duriankari community; ethnographic, very unlikely to contain phonology, listed for completeness.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J. C. 1950s. Unpublished Duriankere wordlist and notes (Voorhoeve 1975 source 'U4'); Anceaux papers, KITLV/Leiden University Library special collections.
